text: The Race: which DIY tool is this?

bank.q: Drives nails in, and its split back end pulls them out
A wooden or rubber-headed hammer for tapping a chisel or tent pegs
Comes in flat-head and Phillips varieties
A bubble in a tube tells you if a shelf is straight
Grips the flats of a nut to turn it
Two pivoting jaws for gripping, bending and snipping wire
A fine-toothed saw held taut in a frame, made for cutting metal
A sharp-edged blade you tap with a mallet to carve or shape wood
Pushed along a plank to shave off thin curls and leave it smooth and flat
A sheet with a gritty surface, graded by numbers like 80 or 240
A coiled metal strip that springs back into its case
An L-shaped hexagonal bar that comes free with flat-pack furniture
Bolted to a workbench, its jaws hold your work tight while you saw
A long iron bar with a flattened end for prising things open
A small pointed tool for making a starter hole for a screw
Heats up to melt metal and join electrical wires
Fires metal staples into wood to fix fabric or cables
A power saw with a thin up-and-down blade for cutting curves
A fluffy cylinder on a handle for covering walls quickly
A flat pointed blade for spreading mortar when laying bricks

text: The Race: which part of a castle is this?

bank.q: A water-filled ditch dug around the walls
Raised on chains so nobody can cross the ditch
A heavy iron-tipped grille that drops down to seal the gateway
The strongest tower at the heart of the castle, the last place to hold out
Notched walls along the top that defenders shoot through
A narrow gap in the wall for archers to fire from
Openings in the gatehouse ceiling for dropping stones on attackers
The open courtyard inside the castle walls
The man-made earth mound a Norman wooden tower stood on
The fortified entrance building guarding the castle gate
An underground prison cell
The main room where the lord ate, entertained and held court
The outer defensive wall linking the towers
An extra fortified gateway built out in front of the main gate
A medieval toilet that emptied down the outside wall
A small back gate for slipping in and out unseen
Stonework jutting out at the top of the wall, with holes for dropping things on attackers
A small tower sticking out from the corner of a bigger tower or wall
The lord and lady's private upstairs room, away from the noise of the hall
A balcony above the hall where musicians played during feasts
